title: WhoseJob? — choose the visual world
question: Every card shows the same moment: a dark streetlight at 2100 Clarendon Blvd, Arlington, routed to Dominion instead of the county. Keep the rolled direction, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Pole Tag
options.lineage: The stamped aluminum tags, reflective decals and stencilled numbers on Northern Virginia's poles, signal cabinets and street furniture
options.thesis: Every answer is issued as a tag, the way the street already labels who owns what.
options.viewport: Map strip with the pin; the routing trace stamps three checks; the answer lands as a big tag: owner, asset number, one-line why, then Report and Call.
options.risk: Tags must stay a functional label system; one decorative rivet too many and it becomes industrial costume.

raised.raise: Check state is line form, not hue: solid line decided it, dashed line checked but didn't decide, struck line had no data.
One module grid on every screen (4 columns on a phone); nothing floats in leftover space.
List and map are one space: a tag's ID (pole number, route, district) is the same code on the pin and in the list, and tapping jumps between them.
Registration: the pin keeps the same place and scale across all five steps, so the flow reads as one spot being examined.
Shape is level: local, state, utility and federal each have their own tag outline, so levels read in grayscale and for color-blind users.

options.label: Guide Sign
options.lineage: Virginia's highway and street signage: green guide panels, white regulatory plates, Highway Gothic lettering
options.thesis: The answer is a guide sign pointing at the right office.
options.viewport: Pin on the map; the answer is a green guide panel reading 'Dominion Energy ↗' with 'Not Arlington County' on a white plate beneath; checks as small route markers.
options.risk: The most familiar choice and where most civic map apps land; it can look like an official VDOT product, which we are not.

options.label: Report Coupon Book
options.lineage: Jet-age airline ticket wallets: carbon-copy coupons, route arcs, baggage stubs
options.thesis: A report is a ticket: FROM your spot TO the office that fixes it, each step a coupon.
options.viewport: A ticket: FROM 2100 Clarendon Blvd TO Dominion Energy, with the pole number in carbon figures; the three checks as stamped boxes; tear off to send.
options.case: Fuses cleanly (FROM spot TO office is exactly the product) and holds product clarity; loses on audience identification, since airline paper is someone else's world, not the street outside.
options.risk: Reads as retro travel nostalgia if the coupons get ornamental.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.thesis: State drawn as hairlines on a charcoal continuum.
options.viewport: A dark rail with thin colored lines for each check.
options.case: Loses both axes: older residents won't recognize it, and hairlines fight large, legible type.
options.kept: State as line form, not color: solid, dashed and struck lines.

options.label: High-Density Modules
options.thesis: Pack every answer into ruled modules.
options.viewport: A mosaic of small boxed modules.
options.case: Loses both axes: tiny type and density exclude the residents this is for.
options.kept: A strict module grid with no whitespace inflation.

options.label: Event Circle Catalog
options.thesis: A numbered hall grid keyed to a map.
options.viewport: A grid of cells keyed to a hall map.
options.case: Loses both axes: foreign to VA-08 residents, and stamp-size cells hurt legibility.
options.kept: The list and the map are the same space, linked by one code.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: One subject at fixed scale through every stage.
options.viewport: Five registered plates of one spot.
options.case: Loses both axes: bookish mood, nothing to do with fixing streets.
options.kept: Registration: the subject keeps one position and scale across stages.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: Shape is meaning; length is duration.
options.viewport: A vertical staff of symbol blocks.
options.case: Loses both axes: abstract notation the audience can't read.
options.kept: Symbol shape carries meaning, so it reads without color.

canonCard.label: The civic service standard
canonCard.thesis: U.S. Web Design System and GOV.UK patterns, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: White page, blue header, one card with the office, its reason and a blue button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every government form; nothing for a judge to remember.
